extracted.intended_audience: authors of systematic reviews and evidence synthesis researchers (researchers, librarians, students)
extracted.subtask_short: assessing quality and bias in systematic reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for selecting and applying study-level risk-of-bias and quality-assessment tools, and for rating certainty of the body of evidence when conducting a systematic review.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.6.1 Systematically assess the risk of bias, using predefined criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: IOM Standard 3.6.1: Systematically assess the risk of bias, using predefined criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform study-level risk-of-bias assessments using criteria defined a priori in the review protocol so assessments are systematic and reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.6.2 Assess the relevance of the study's populations, interventions, and outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: IOM Standard 3.6.2: Assess the relevance of the study’s populations, interventions, and outcome measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate external validity/applicability by checking whether study populations, interventions, and outcomes match the review question and intended context.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.6.3 Assess the fidelity of the implementation of interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: IOM Standard 3.6.3: Assess the fidelity of the implementation of interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judiciously appraise whether interventions were delivered as intended (implementation fidelity), since poor fidelity can bias effect estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a tool that fits the study designs included in your systematic review
rubrics_metrics.description: To assess risk of bias/quality you will need a tool that fits the study designs included in your systematic review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select tools appropriate to the study types in your review (see searchable spreadsheet and LATITUDES library). Downloadable resources and training materials can help match tools to designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a method to conduct the assessment in a dual-blind manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a method to conduct the assessment in a dual-blind manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for independent, blinded assessments (typically two reviewers independently) with predefined processes for resolving disagreements (consensus or third reviewer). Document who assessed what and how disagreements were resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: RoB 2.0 — Randomized Controlled Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: RoB 2.0 — risk-of-bias tool for randomized controlled trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RoB 2.0 for assessing bias in RCTs (domains include randomization process, deviations from intended interventions, missing outcome data, measurement of the outcome, selection of the reported result).

rubrics_metrics.name: ROBINS-I — Non-randomized (observational) studies of interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: ROBINS-I — for non-randomized (observational) studies or cohorts of interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply ROBINS-I to assess bias in non-randomized studies estimating effects of interventions; consider pre-specified confounding and selection biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROBINS-E — Non-randomized studies of exposures (environmental/occupational)
rubrics_metrics.description: ROBINS-E — for non-randomized (observational) studies or cohorts of exposures other than interventions, including environmental and occupational exposures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ROBINS-E when assessing observational studies focused on exposures rather than interventions; attend to exposure assessment and confounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) — Case control or cohort studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) — for case control or cohort studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NOS to appraise selection, comparability, and exposure/outcome assessment in cohort and case-control studies; be aware of its scoring approach and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: QUADAS-2 — Diagnostic accuracy studies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply QUADAS-2 to evaluate risk of bias and applicability in studies of diagnostic test accuracy across patient selection, index test, reference standard, and flow/timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: AXIS — Cross-sectional/prevalence studies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AXIS to assess methodological quality of cross-sectional designs, focusing on sampling, measurement, and reporting aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) — Mixed-methods reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) — for mixed-methods systematic reviews with a variety of study types including both qualitative & quantitative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MMAT supports concurrent appraisal across qualitative, quantitative, and mixed-method studies in a single instrument when reviews include heterogeneous designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: IHE Case Series Studies Critical Appraisal Checklist — Case series
rubrics_metrics.description: IHE Case Series Studies Critical Appraisal Checklist — for case series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the IHE case series checklist to appraise design, selection, outcome ascertainment, and reporting in case series.

rubrics_metrics.name: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Case Reports — Case reports
rubrics_metrics.description: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Case Reports — for case reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the JBI checklist to examine the quality and completeness of single case reports when they are included in evidence synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: QualSyst — Standard quality assessment criteria for a variety of fields
rubrics_metrics.description: QualSyst — STANDARD QUALITY ASSESSMENT CRITERIA for Evaluating Primary Research Papers from a Variety of Fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use QualSyst when synthesizing primary research across diverse fields; it provides generic criteria adaptable across study types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Levels of Evidence and strength of recommendation taxonomies (Oxford CEBM, SORT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Levels of Evidence and Grades of Recommendations (e.g., Oxford-Centre for Evidence Based Medicine; SORT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider applying established evidence-level hierarchies to describe the strength of individual studies and to inform recommendation grading; be aware of differences between systems and choose one appropriate to your field.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE — assess certainty of the body of evidence at the outcome level
rubrics_metrics.description: GRADE (Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations) is a transparent framework for developing and presenting summaries of evidence and provides a systematic approach for making clinical practice recommendations. PRISMA 2020 requests an assessment of the certainty of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use GRADE to rate certainty (confidence) in effect estimates at the outcome level (not the individual study level). GRADE defines four levels: High, Moderate, Low, Very low, with explicit interpretations: High = very confident; Moderate = moderately confident; Low = low confidence; Very low = any estimate is very uncertain. Note: while GRADE considers risk of bias as part of downgrading, you still need study-level risk-of-bias tools to inform GRADE judgements.
